<!-- pr-reviewer: 5a9551562879c98123b39d75cca4732d159f541c -->
**Verdict: ready for the maintainer to merge.** This was a safety-tier review, because the PR changes posted G-code motion at program end.

I trial-merged the PR head `5a955156` with `main` `a6562c35` locally. It merged cleanly; `tormach.cps` auto-merged with main's #931 work-offset change.

### What looks good
- **The program end is the user's Hub choice C.** `onClose` now ends `M9` (only if coolant ran), `M5`, `G53 G0 Z<safe>`, the EndUnits word, `M30`. There is no trailing `G30` and no `G0 A0` (`assets/posts/tormach.cps:990`).
- **The refactor is small.** `liftZ()` (`tormach.cps:289`) is the one `G53 G0 Z` lift, and `retract()` (`:302`) adds the tool-change `G30` on top of it. The tool-change output is byte-identical to before.
- **The golden diff is exactly as claimed.** I scripted a check over every changed `*.nc`. It requires each file's only change to be a single removed `G30` line, and it prints that line's context in the base.
  - Result: 33 files, 33 removed `-G30` lines, 0 added lines, 0 other changes.
  - Every removed line sat in the same `G53 G0 Z0 | G30 | M30` end block.
  - The check gives the same result on the PR commit alone and on the trial merge with main.
  - The lathe and plasma goldens are untouched. Each Tormach mill golden still has exactly one `G30`: its tool change.
- **Hygiene is complete.** `fix(post):` subject, `Fixes #1594`, a `Changelog:` line that says the posted output changes, and a decision file at `docs/decisions/1594-tormach-end-g53.md`. There is no `PROCESS_VERSION` edit (none is needed), no `CHANGELOG.md` edit and no snapshot PNGs. The new test file has a provenance line and a gate map.

### Local results (merged with main, macOS, debug)
| What | Result |
|---|---|
| `camcraft-post`, every suite (lib + 50 test binaries, `script_tormach`, `recorded_streams`, `ream_cycle` and `probe_tormach` among them) | all ok, 0 failed |
| app `tormach_program_end` | 3 passed |
| app `tormach_post` / `tormach_safe_retract` / `tormach_end_units` / `tormach_fourth_axis` | 10 / 4 / 7 / 12 passed |
| app `tormach_machines` / `tormach_routers` / `microarc_test_part` / `recorded_post_streams` | 6 / 5 / 2 / 5 passed |
| app `posting` / `conformance` / `program_units` / `post_unit_word` / `fourth_axis_pose` / `rotary_feed_cap` | 17 / 7 / 7 / 5 / 9 / 11 passed |
| app `probe_op` / `control_comp` / `coolant_air` / `program_comments` / `program_entry` / `program_info` | 12 / 5 / 4 / 4 / 9 / 10 passed |
| app `rigid_tapping` / `post_cycle_feed_spindle` / `probe_no_coolant` / `probe_spindle_range` / `wear_comp` / `solid_law_goldens` / `units_migrate` | 5 / 8 / 5 / 3 / 5 / 7 / 5 passed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings` | clean |

I ran these app suites because they are the ones that read the Tormach goldens. The quick-gate plan wanted every app suite (shared golden inputs changed); the PR body reports a full green run of that plan.

### Mutation check of the pins
I applied each mutation to `tormach.cps`, ran the suites, and restored the file. Every mutation was killed.

| Mutation | `tormach_program_end` pins that go red | Other suites |
|---|---|---|
| M1: end calls `retract()` again (G30 back) | `every_tormach_mill_…`, `a_fourth_axis_…` | safe_retract, end_units, tormach_post, microarc_test_part, script_tormach red |
| M2: `G0 A0` after the end lift | all 3 | same as M1 |
| M3: drop the tool-change `G30` | `every_tormach_mill_…` | safe_retract, tormach_post, microarc, script_tormach red |
| M4: end with `G30` only, no lift | all 3 | same as M1 |
| M5: no end lift at all | all 3 | same as M1 |
| M6: end lift hard-coded to `Z0`, ignoring the stated safe Z | `a_stated_safe_z_…` | safe_retract red |

### Requested before merge
None.

### Questions / notes (not blocking)
1. **M5 before the lift is safe, and this PR does not change the order.**
   - `M5` already came before `G53 G0 Z0` (it comes from `endPreamble()`, `tormach.cps:465`).
   - The last motion before `onClose` is the operation's own retract out of the cut, so the spindle stops with the tool already clear. For example, `drill_plate.nc` has `G80`, `G0 … Z0.1969`, `M9`, `M5`, and `index_4face_microarc4.nc` has `G0 … Z1.5748`, then `M9`, `M5`.
   - The lift that follows is a straight-up move in machine Z, so a stopped tool never moves sideways or down.
   - Neither Tormach's PathPilot post-processor guidelines (knowledgebase.tormach.com/8l/pathpilot-post-processor-guidelines) nor the LinuxCNC G-code reference prescribe an order. They only define M5 as spindle stop and M30 as end-and-rewind. Retract to clearance, then M5, then home Z is ordinary practice.
   - Keeping it is right.
2. **Where the safe Z comes from.**
   - `safeZ()` (`tormach.cps:268`) takes the machine file's Z `safe_retract`. Every shipped Tormach mill states `0.0` (770M/M+/MX/MX-ML/microARC 4, 1100M/M+/MX, 1500MX, 24R), and machine Z0 is the top of travel on a Tormach.
   - An unnamed machine, or one named Tormach, with no stated value falls back to 0.
   - Any other machine with no stated value is refused by name and gets no `G53` line at all. That case is pinned by `a_non_tormach_machine_without_a_safe_z_is_refused_by_name`.
   - Pre-existing gap: `crates/post/src/machine/parse.rs:359` accepts any finite `safe_retract` and does not check it against the Z travel. A typo such as `-5` would post `G53 G0 Z-5` at both the tool change and the end. This is not new here; it could be a P7 follow-up.
3. **The 4th axis.**
   - With no A return, A stays where the last operation left it.
   - That is safe for the next program: `endPreamble` clears `aNow`/`aSection`, and every section restates `G53 G0 Z0` then `G0 A..` after its `T.. M6` before any XY move (`index_4face_microarc4.nc:16-18`). The next program therefore states A, with Z at the top, before it cuts.
4. **The tool-change `G30` (#1596): I think P7 understates it.**
   - In every 3-axis Tormach program, the first tool change is `G53 G0 Z0`, `G30`, `T.. M6`, `G43 H..`, `S.. M3`, `M8`, then **`G0 X.. Y..` with no Z lift in between**. See `drill_plate.nc:7-14` and `probe_guard_moves.nc:7-12`.
   - With a stored G30 below the part top, like the Hub sim's (machine Z -1.5611, below the part top in the #1594 run), the tool drops to the G30 point. It then rapids sideways at that height to the first XY, which can cross the vise or the part.
   - This happens on every program, mid-program changes included. The 4th-axis sections are protected only because they re-lift before `G0 A`.
   - That is a collision the post emits without a warning, which the AGENTS.md table rates `P1` (or `P3` at least, if "keep SETG30 at the top of Z" counts as the workaround). The kit README already tells operators to do exactly that.
   - A low-risk fix would be a `G53 G0 Z<safe>` after the `G43 H..` line, before the first XY rapid. That works whatever G30 holds.
   - The maintainer should decide the rating. It does not block this PR, which only removes one instance of the risk.
5. **Golden overlap with #1577.** Four goldens are touched by both PRs: `tormach/contour_disc_hole.nc`, `tormach/contour_plate_with_hole.nc`, `tormach/contour_tangential_lead.nc` and `inch/tormach/contour_plate_with_hole.nc`. Whichever merges second regenerates them.
6. **Not exercised here:** a Hub or machine run of CamCraft-posted output with this ending (the PR says so). The user's hand-written program C is the reference.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

Post-merge note (the PR was merged before this review was posted). Verdict: no blockers found.

What looks good
- Post change is small: `onClose` now calls `liftZ()` (G53 G0 Z<safe>) instead of `retract()`; `retract()` (tool change only) is `liftZ()` + the unchanged G30 block. Order at program end stays endPreamble (G80, M9 when coolant ran, M5) -> G53 G0 Z -> optional EndUnits G20/G21 -> M30. The machine-coordinate Z lift is the last motion; no XY or rotary move follows it, no G0 A0.
- Reading against public docs: G53 is a non-modal machine-coordinate move that ignores the tool length offset and work offsets; a bare G30 without axis words moves every axis to the stored G30 position (LinuxCNC params 5181-5189), which is the hazard the user reproduced in Hub. Dropping the trailing G30 removes that. The Z value goes through `fu()` (units) and is Z0 or the machine's stated safe Z (#495), so a non-zero stated safe Z still ends there.
- Goldens: 33 files changed, the diff is exactly 33 lines `-G30` and nothing else (checked with `git diff --no-renames origin/main...pr -- '*.nc'`). Spot-checked index_4face_microarc4 (ends M9, M5, G53 G0 Z0, M30) and probe_corner (M5, G53 G0 Z0, M30): no XY/A move after the lift. Lathe and plasma goldens untouched.
- New `crates/app/tests/tormach_program_end.rs` has three pins (every mill machine ends M5/G53 G0 Z0/M30 with nothing but M30 after; stated safe Z; 4th-axis job ends with no G0 A). Author reports mutation checks (restoring the end G30 turns them red). The three updated suites assert the new ending.
- Diff touches no Cargo.toml, build.rs, .github, scripts, .cargo, toolchain or xtask path (checked). Decision file, `Changelog:` line, `Fixes #1594` (diff fixes the mill end, the issue's scope; plasma/lathe split to #1596) all present. No Process-change files, no snapshot PNGs, no CHANGELOG edit. Provenance: PR cites LinuxCNC docs and the user's own Hub run only.

Results merged with main
- On the self-hosted runner: https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/actions/runs/43533981903 - success (quick gate and clippy). Not run locally.

Requested before merge
- None so far.

Questions / notes (not blocking). No posted file was run on a real control or PathPilot Hub.
1. Not run on a real control or PathPilot Hub with a CamCraft-posted file; the evidence is the user's hand-written ending C (the PR says so under "Not exercised"). Worth one real run by the maintainer.
2. The program end does not cancel G49 (tool length offset stays active at M30). Unchanged from before, and M30 resets offsets per the #596 comment, but G53 ignores TLO anyway, so the lift height is the same.
3. The tool-change `G53 G0 Z0` then `G30` keeps the same low-G30 risk the PR fixed at the end; noted by the author as follow-up #1596 (that issue names plasma/lathe; the mill tool-change case is described in the PR body, consider naming it in #1596 explicitly).

Merged already; this is a post-merge note.
